newsitem.title: USA: Ill. governor signs Chicago airport takeover bill.
newsitem.headline: Ill. governor signs Chicago airport takeover bill.

text.p: - Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar signed into law on Monday a bill allowing the state to take over a small airport in Chicago.

However, the bill, which was passed by the Republican controlled legislature earlier this month, does not take effect until June 1,1997 because the passage lacked a required three-fifths vote of lawmakers for immediate effect.

Republicans reportedly are considering holding another vote on the bill when they return to session early next month. An affirmative vote after the new year would automatically give the bill immediate effect without a super-majority vote of lawmakers.
The bill signing was the latest volley to be fired in the fight over Meigs Field on Chicago's downtown lakefront.

Edgar wants the now shuttered airport to remain open for business and state planes while Chicago Mayor Richard Daley wants to bulldoze the airport to make way for a $27 million bond-financed nature park.
In a statement issued on Monday, Edgar's press secretary Mike Lawrence said the governor is "hopeful the issue will be resolved through compromise."
A spokesperson for Daley was not immediately available to comment on the bill signing.

Meanwhile, oral arguments were scheduled for Monday morning before the Illinois Appellate Court on the state's appeal of a Cook County Circuit Court's ruling that sided with Chicago's plans for the airport.
